title: a-mailbox-nobody-reads-keeps-nothing
intention: A discovered device's mailbox keeps no mail it has no reader for: _FeedbackDevice.receive writes to the inbound DataRecorder only when RECORDER_ON_READ is declared, and still accepts the mail.
why: Measured 2026-10-01: test_isolation reds at 273MB against its 150MB bound, blocking every tester PROVED crossing; discovered devices' mailboxes keep inbound mail no reader opens. Lived symptom: no tester ticket can reach PROVED.
traces_to: Law 9 and Law 7: test_isolation reds because instance-space is inflated by mail nobody reads, and that red blocks every PROVED crossing in the tester component. The ruling 'if it's not consumed, it's trash' (2026-09-30).
how: In cairn/devices/cairn/machines/ground_loop/discovered.py _FeedbackDevice.receive: when type(self).RECORDER_ON_READ is None, skip the DataRecorder write and return the same accepted reply. Update the comment above RECORDER_READ_FREQUENCY_SECONDS/RECORDER_ON_READ: undeclared now means unkept, citing the ruling 'if it's not consumed, it's trash' (2026-09-30, CairnCommons/intentions-not-beside-code/I-heartbeat-probes-and-bus.md) and the sibling ae8d2bfb08e2. Proved by a new cairn/devices/cairn/machines/ground_loop/proofs/test_a_mailbox_nobody_reads_keeps_nothing.py over a _FeedbackDevice whose _recorder is preset to a scratch DataRecorder. The one-time drain of already-filled undeclared inbound recorders is the sibling's apply, not repeated here.
falsifier: RED if: (1) a _FeedbackDevice with RECORDER_ON_READ None, its _recorder preset to a scratch DataRecorder, receives one envelope and the scratch recorder then holds any record; (2) a _FeedbackDevice subclass declaring RECORDER_ON_READ 'hold' and RECORDER_READ_FREQUENCY_SECONDS 60 receives one envelope and the scratch recorder does not hold exactly one record carrying that envelope's id; (3) either receive does not return accepted True with the device id. Horizon: the tester seal of the new proof.
watchme: none, because cairn/devices/tester/proofs/test_isolation.py is the receiver: its disk_bytes bound reds at every reseal while instance-space carries unread mail, and the build gate reads it at every PROVED crossing in the tester component
children: none, because the change is one guard in _FeedbackDevice.receive in cairn/devices/cairn/machines/ground_loop/discovered.py
builder_notes: A Haiku builder would ask: (1) How is the fixture built? from cairn.devices.cairn.machines.ground_loop.discovered import _FeedbackDevice resolved inside each tooth; dev = _FeedbackDevice('mailbox_fixture'); dev._recorder = DataRecorder(scratch_dir('mailbox_fixture_') / 'inbound', expected_read_frequency_seconds=..., on_read=...). (2) The declared case: a subclass class _Declared(_FeedbackDevice): RECORDER_ON_READ = 'hold'; RECORDER_READ_FREQUENCY_SECONDS = 60. (3) Envelope: {'id': 'env-fixture-1', 'sender': 'proof', 'why': 'fixture mail', 'verb': '', 'body': {'k': 1}}. (4) scratch_dir comes from cairn.devices.tester.scratch. (5) PROVES = {ticket: {'1':..., '2':..., '3':...}}.
